humanities_role_explanation: Evaluates LLM domain-specific competence in diplomatic transcription and period-specific orthographic preservation of 18th-century Russian Civil font, assessing historical errors like temporal conflation and over-historicization.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Evaluates multimodal LLMs by providing scanned images of historical pages or lines along with textual prompts to generate structured textual transcriptions.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Diplomatic transcription of historical 18th-century Russian Civil font, visual recognition of obsolete/period-specific Cyrillic characters and layouts from page scans, and post-OCR textual correction.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Scoped specifically to historical document OCR and diplomatic transcription of 18th-century Russian Civil font texts.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: Evaluates 12 generative multimodal LLMs, including GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, Claude 3.5/3.7, Gemini 2.0/2.5, and Qwen-2.5-VL.

quantitative_metrics.note: Uses standard OCR metrics (CER, WER, CaseER) alongside novel domain-specific metrics (Historical Character Preservation Rate, Archaic Insertion Rate).

summary: This paper establishes a comprehensive evaluation framework for LLM-based historical document OCR, utilizing a novel dataset of 18th-century Russian Civil font prints. The authors introduce domain-specific metrics (HCPR and AIR) to evaluate historical orthographic accuracy and reveal temporal biases in generative models.
key_findings: Gemini-2.5-Pro and Qwen-2.5-VL emerged as the most stable and accurate models, substantially outperforming traditional OCR tools. However, the study identifies a systematic 'over-historicization' bias where models inappropriately insert obsolete pre-Petrine characters. Additionally, post-OCR text correction using LLMs degraded rather than improved the transcription quality.
paper_name: Evaluating LLMs for Historical Document OCR: A Methodological Framework for Digital Humanities
facets_explanation: The reference ground truth was created through a multi-stage process where initial OCR generated by a fine-tuned TrOCR model was subjected to 100% manual correction and a two-pass protocol by a single expert annotator to ensure diplomatic fidelity. The transcription task relies entirely on the provided document images without requiring external historical knowledge. Models are evaluated by comparing their outputs to this single gold-standard reference using distance metrics like CER and WER. While the authors report a high exact-match rate from an audit by a second verifier, the paper does not discuss how or whether divergences between annotators were resolved.
review_notes_incremental: Ciop and Cip disagreed on plurality_treatment (Ciop: noise, Cip: not_addressed). Resolved to 'not_addressed' because while the paper reports inter-annotator agreement on an audit sample to validate accuracy, it does not explicitly discuss treating divergence as noise or filtering it out.
